findings.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey joins userUID, action, name, and parent with the same "_" delimiter, so different (name, parent) pairs can produce an identical key (e.g. name="foo_bar",parent="baz" vs name="foo",parent="bar_baz"), letting a cached denial for one resource incorrectly short-circuit Check() to deny an unrelated resource

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — permDenialCache key is built from the raw, unresolved checkReq.UserUID subject value instead of the canonical UID returned by GetUserIdentifiers, unlike userPermCacheKey/idCache/teamCache/basicRoleCache which all key off the resolved userIdentifiers.UID; since GetUserIdentifiers explicitly supports numeric-ID vs UID subjects resolving to the same user, the same identity checked via different subject formats gets incoherent, non-shared denial-cache entries

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:124 — permissionCacheUsage metric is only recorded "true" when the cached-permission fast path yields allowed=true; a genuine cache hit that resolves to allowed=false (or an identifier-lookup error from getCachedIdentityPermissions) falls through to the unconditional "false" increment at line 137, making cache-hit-rate telemetry for this caching-improvement PR inaccurate

pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:241 — NoopCache's methods use receiver name "lc" (short for LocalCache), a copy-paste leftover from the real LocalCache implementation that is misleading on a type literally named NoopCache.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey mints one cache entry per (namespace,userUID,action,resourceName,parentFolder) instead of per (user,action) like permCache, and this Service cache is backed by cache.NewLocalCache(cache.Config{Expiry, CleanupInterval}) (pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:88) which only expires entries by TTL/cleanup sweep with no visible max-entry/LRU size bound, so a burst of Check calls across many distinct dashboards/folders for one user can grow memory well beyond the old per-(user,action) footprint within each 30s window

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cached permissions but checkPermission on them evaluates to false, Check() still falls through to fetch full permissions via getIdentityPermissions and calls checkPermission again, duplicating potentially expensive checkInheritedPermissions/buildFolderTree scope-traversal work for the same request

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — permDenialCache key is built from the raw, unresolved checkReq.UserUID subject value instead of the canonical UID returned by GetUserIdentifiers, unlike userPermCacheKey/idCache/teamCache/basicRoleCache which all key off the resolved userIdentifiers.UID; since GetUserIdentifiers explicitly supports numeric-ID vs UID subjects resolving to the same user, the same identity checked via different subject formats gets incoherent, non-shared denial-cache entries

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the new denial-cache key is computed as `userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, ...)` (service.go around the added block near line 111). Unlike `permCache` lookups in `getCachedIdentityPermissions`, which resolve the subject via `GetUserIdentifiers(...)` and then key by `userIdentifiers.UID`, the denial cache never canonicalizes `checkReq.UserUID`. This makes denial caching inconsistent for the same underlying user when `checkReq.UserUID` can vary in representation (e.g., numeric ID vs UID), so a deny cached for one representation won’t be hit for the other and can be bypassed by the cached-permissions fast path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:124 — permissionCacheUsage metric is only recorded "true" when the cached-permission fast path yields allowed=true; a genuine cache hit that resolves to allowed=false (or an identifier-lookup error from getCachedIdentityPermissions) falls through to the unconditional "false" increment at line 137, making cache-hit-rate telemetry for this caching-improvement PR inaccurate

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, a cache hit that results in allowed==false is not counted as a cache hit: when getCachedIdentityPermissions returns err==nil but checkPermission returns allowed==false, the code does not increment permissionCacheUsage("true", action) and then falls through to the unconditional permissionCacheUsage("false", action).Inc() just before calling getIdentityPermissions. Also, any non-cache-miss error from getCachedIdentityPermissions (e.g., GetUserIdentifiers error) will likewise be recorded as "false". This makes the permissionCacheUsage metric inaccurate as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:241 — NoopCache's methods use receiver name "lc" (short for LocalCache), a copy-paste leftover from the real LocalCache implementation that is misleading on a type literally named NoopCache.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `type NoopCache struct{}` with methods using receiver name `lc` (e.g., `func (lc *NoopCache) Get...`). However, this is purely a naming/style nit (receiver identifier) and does not indicate a defect or substantive review issue grounded in behavior; the methods correctly implement a no-op cache (returning `cache.ErrNotFound` on Get and nil on Set/Delete).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey mints one cache entry per (namespace,userUID,action,resourceName,parentFolder) instead of per (user,action) like permCache, and this Service cache is backed by cache.NewLocalCache(cache.Config{Expiry, CleanupInterval}) (pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:88) which only expires entries by TTL/cleanup sweep with no visible max-entry/LRU size bound, so a burst of Check calls across many distinct dashboards/folders for one user can grow memory well beyond the old per-(user,action) footprint within each 30s window

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a new negative cache keyed by `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace,userUID,action,name,parent)` (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go) and in `Service.Check` it unconditionally `Set`s an entry on every denied check (`s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true)`) and short-circuits future checks on `Get` hits. This is higher-cardinality than the existing `permCache` which is per-(user,action). The diff also shows use of `cache.NewLocalCache(cache.Config{Expiry, CleanupInterval})` without any max-size/LRU bound (e.g., in tests via `setupService`, and similarly in `newRemoteRBACClient`), so within the TTL window a burst of distinct (name,parent) denials can accumulate more entries than before. This is a concrete performance/memory-growth concern grounded in the new keying scheme, though not a guaranteed correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — When getCachedIdentityPermissions returns cached permissions but checkPermission on them evaluates to false, Check() still falls through to fetch full permissions via getIdentityPermissions and calls checkPermission again, duplicating potentially expensive checkInheritedPermissions/buildFolderTree scope-traversal work for the same request

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check(), after a cache hit (getCachedIdentityPermissions returns perms, err == nil), it calls s.checkPermission(ctx, cachedPerms, checkReq). If that evaluates to false, it does not return; it falls through to fetch fresh permissions via s.getIdentityPermissions(...) and then calls s.checkPermission(ctx, permissions, checkReq) again (see the new block starting around `cachedPerms, err := ...` and the later `permissions, err := ...` block). This is a real diff-grounded duplication of work; while not a correctness defect (it may be intended to handle stale caches), it can add avoidable CPU/IO if checkPermission performs expensive scope traversal.
